nations.name: Rappahannock Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the lower Rappahannock and Mattaponi river watersheds in Virginia, as described by the Tribe's environmental department

facts.text: The Tribe describes its homeland as including the lower Rappahannock and Mattaponi river watersheds.

source.title: Department Of Environmental Services | Rappahannock Indian Tribe

facts.evidence: the lower Rappahannock and Mattaponi river watersheds

facts.text: The Tribe's history describes repeated forced removals before a return to ancestral homelands downriver, where its community continues.
facts.evidence: returned to their ancestral homelands downriver

facts.text: The Tribe dates its incorporation to 1921 as part of efforts to strengthen its government and seek recognition.
The Tribe's environmental department says it coordinates the Return to the River youth program.

source.title: Department Of Environmental Services | Rappahannock Indian Tribe

facts.evidence: Coordinates the Tribe’s Return to the River youth program.

nations.name: Monacan Indian Nation
nations.lands: Bear Mountain in Amherst County, Virginia; the Nation describes ancestral homelands extending through Virginia and parts of West Virginia and North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation describes its citizens as descendants of Virginia and North Carolina Eastern Siouan cultural and linguistic groups.
facts.evidence: Eastern Siouan cultural and linguistic groups

facts.text: The Nation's history says Virginia's 1924 Racial Integrity Law led state officials to change Monacan records without their knowledge.
facts.evidence: records being changed by state officials

facts.text: The Nation dates the Episcopal Church's return of a deed for 7.5 acres of land to 1995.
The Nation says its Priority Climate Action Plan includes a greenhouse gas inventory to guide conservation and emissions-reduction work.
